note: Theme-agnostic N64-era look convention shared by every pack, kit build and future style profile (docs/N64-LOOK-CONVENTIONS.md). Packs supply colours and environment data; they inherit these rules and may only override a rule through an explicit view.json "n64" block. Runtime copy: theme.json "n64" (adventure_maker/assets_v3.runtime_snapshot).

output.note: Fixed 320x240 framebuffer, 4:3, shown 3x with bilinear (no sharpening); polygon edges antialiased like the RDP coverage AA. PS1-style vertex snapping and affine texture warp are never used (perspective-correct texturing).

filtering.note: n64 = three-point (triangle) filtering when magnified, the mip chain only when minified, biased by lod_bias toward detail (distant ground keeps its painted blotches without unmipmapped sparkle); the same soft filter on characters (unmipmapped, so face atlas cells never average).

lamp_pool.note: soft radial floor decal under an emitter (painted light), not a per-pixel circle

halo.note: soft glow billboard around a lamp (N64 lantern/torch glow sprite), a few times the shade's size; no screen-space bloom and no room-sized halos

chrome.note: chrome/glass = painted sphere-map texture lit by the room rig; no white-hot boosts or fresnel catch

actor.note: characters use the world rig; a modest second directional (kicker) from behind the subject is the only extra

lighting.note: Gouraud: baked vertex colour x (ambient + sky/ground hemisphere + key + fill + up to 4 point lights), evaluated per vertex. Point lights on static surfaces are sampled on a virtual vertex lattice of lattice_m metres and interpolated (the look of vertex light on a tessellated N64 floor: soft polygonal pools, no per-pixel circles, no wedges across big triangles). Gloss/chrome env lookups use per-vertex sphere-map texgen. The room value structure (darker ceilings, wall-base contact shadow) is a smooth baked-lightmap-like term. No PBR, no per-pixel lights, no real-time specular, no fresnel rim.

fog.note: Linear distance fog evaluated per vertex. Exteriors: the painted sky melts into the fog colour across sky_horizon = [from, to] (sin of the view elevation relative to the top of the far terrain seen from the room camera, presenter.fit_sky_horizon), so the visible horizon and the fogged distance share one colour. Interiors: fog colour = the room's darkest ambient tone, close enough to soften the far wall.

interior_cool.note: blue futuristic, cool but restrained: pearl/cobalt values, no neon, sparing warm practicals

interior_warm.note: cottage, warm natural: soft warm key, cool-ish fill in the shadows, warm window light

exterior_day.note: village daylight/dusk: painted sky gradient, fog tinted to the horizon

exterior_night.note: night snow field: painted aurora sky, pale snow, fog tinted to the horizon

texel_density.note: Texels per metre by material class (texture size / tile_m). Same class = same density in every pack, so a scene reads at one consistent texel scale. Flat, emissive, view-plane, env and character roles are outside the table.

vertex_variation.note: painted low-frequency light/dark patches in the baked vertex colour of large terrain roles (deterministic value noise of the vertex position, +-amount of the light ramp): N64 artists broke up big cliff and ground faces with vertex colour, not with texture detail

textures.note: Hand-painted look with palette-exact texels. Fields keep their mid-frequency painted structure and are quantized to the pack ramp with an IRREGULAR mottle threshold (seeded, rank-equalised white noise) instead of the regular 4x4 Bayer grid, so band transitions read as painted mottling that three-point filtering turns into the soft blotchy look of N64 textures (fully clean bands were tried in round 2: frames went posterised-flat, 0.36-0.52 near-uniform, beyond the defect gate). Readable textures (crisp_gens) are quantized clean. Sky/window scene cards paint their aurora/cloud/haze layers into the gradient with soft masks (painted_sky). A recipe may set `dither` (amount or false), `dither_pattern` (bayer/mottle), `soften` (wrapped blur passes) or `painted` explicitly.

gate.note: n64_fidelity section (adventure_maker/n64_gate.py). Thresholds calibrated so the round-0 renders (before this convention, commit 80d5236) fail and private N64 study references (downscaled to 320x240: crisp 0.00-0.23, clip <= 0.002) pass where comparable; they are additions, never loosened defect-gate thresholds. Calibration numbers: docs/N64-FIDELITY-AUDIT.md.

library.note: Texture library checks (n64_gate library). density_spread_max = 1 + texel_density.tolerance (every role of a class within 25% of the others; round 0 had 1.33-8x). hf_energy_max / median: per-texel energy of each generated texture, readable text/screens exempt; calibrated so the round-0 library (commit 80d5236: worst texture 0.188, village median 0.0525) fails. Known-bad control: tests/fixtures/n64fidelity/library-round0.
